# Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformers: Architecture, Training, and Deployment

Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a paradigm that decouples model capacity from computational cost. In standard dense transformers, every token activates every parameter. In MoE, only a small subset of parameters (the "active experts") are engaged per token, enabling massive model scaling while maintaining inference FLOPs comparable to smaller dense models.

## 1. Architectural Core

### 1.1 Basic Structure
An MoE layer replaces a standard feed-forward network (FFN) in a transformer block with a parallel ensemble of $N$ expert networks $\{E_1, \dots, E_N\}$, each typically a 2-layer MLP:

$$
E_k(\mathbf{x}) = W_{k,2} \cdot \text{ReLU}(W_{k,1} \mathbf{x} + b_{k,1}) + b_{k,2}
$$
